summary: E. W. Adikaram worked in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of London (attested 1946), where he studied under William Stede.

Eberhard Sandschneider studied at Saarland University (~1976–1986). A specialist in Sinology and other fields, he held posts at Mainz (1995–1998), the Free University of Berlin (1998), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Working in Indology and philosophy, Edeltraud Harzer studied at Charles University and the University of Washington (PhD), and under traditional teachers Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Puget Sound, Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin (1998).

Edith Wyschogrod was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Hunter College (~1953–1957) and Columbia University (~1965–1970) and served on the faculty at Rice University (~1992–2003).
Edmond Yee is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He served on the faculty at both Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union (~1990–2008).

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studying at Heidelberg (~1872–1875) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He was Professor of Philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and professor of Indian languages and comparative religions at Fribourg (~1893–1898).

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and other fields, studying at Clare College, King's College, the LSE, and under Bronislaw Malinowski (~1937–1939). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1953 to 1979.
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist who graduated from Harvard University in 1886. He studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2015, he held posts as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Berthold Delbrück (~1891–1893). He held academic posts at the University of Kiel (~1913–1917), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1917–1924), and the University of Göttingen (~1924–1940).

Eduard Müller was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University (~1872–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern from ~1886 to 1908.

Eduard Sachau worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Kiel and Leipzig (under Hermann Brockhaus), he held posts at Vienna, Frederick William University Berlin, and as Director of the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Frederick William University Berlin. He held professorial posts at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach studied Buddhist studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), earning a Master of Buddhist Studies under the supervision of Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
Edward Albert Gait was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1880–1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Charterhouse School and Merton College, he served as Professor of Hindústání at East India Company College (~1845–1857) and in the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he was Principal of Sanskrit College (1858–1864), taught history at Presidency University, and served as Professor at Cambridge (1867, 1887).
Edward C. Dimock specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1950–1953) and held a post at the University of Chicago from ~1957 to 1992.

Edward Clive Bayley worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College / East India Company College (~1840–1842) and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Cologne (PhD) and Bonn. He held posts at London, Lancaster, Washington, and UC Berkeley, and served as Vice-President of the Buddhist Society (~1953–1970).
